Troops of Operation Enduring Peace have arrested a suspected fake soldier in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State for alleged phone snatching and public disturbance. The arrest was confirmed on Monday in an interview with our correspondent in Jos, the state capital, by the Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force, Operation Enduring Peace, Capt. Chinonso Oteh. “Yes, it is true. That one happened in the Jos North area,” Oteh affirmed. He further said the troops arrested the suspect, identified as Salim Idris, at about 11:30 am on October 25 at Filin Sukuwa in Jos North LGA. According to him, the arrest followed credible intelligence about the suspect’s alleged criminal activities in the area. Army clarifies encounter with police in Plateau, seeks public cooperation Kwankwaso faults Tinubu on insecurity, poverty 2027: Police promise adequate security in Plateau He said the troops trailed the suspect and apprehended him while dressed in a military camouflage uniform. “Preliminary interrogation reportedly revealed that the suspect had been involved in a series of alleged criminal activities, including public disturbance, phone snatching and impersonation of security agencies,” he stated. It was learnt that the suspect is currently in the custody of troops while further investigation continues James Abraham
